title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-10-12
content:
Infrastructure Weekly Update  2026-10-12
Owner: Priya Raman (eng-infrastructure)
Contributors: Liam Chen, Sofia Martinez, Ethan Park
Status: Draft

Executive summary:
- Fleet utilization remains elevated as a mix of Hosted API and Dedicated customers scale up for Q4 launches. Total GPU utilization (weighted) averaged 82% across all regions last week (up from 74% two weeks ago).
- We brought two H100 pods online in us-west1 and one in eu-west1 which relieved short-term queuing for long-context workloads but introduced a driver regression that required a rolling rollback on eu-west1.
- Autoscaler tuning (scale-down policies) rolled out to apac1 reduced noisy-node churn but highlighted several under-provisioned AZs for Dedicated capacity.

Key metrics (week of 2026-10-05 -> 2026-10-11):
- Weighted GPU utilization: 82% (hosted: 76%, dedicated: 90%)
- Average queue latency (tail p95 for long-context generation): 460ms (target 300ms)
- Average cost per 1K tokens (in-hosted): $2.90 (after recent batching improvements)
- Spot preemption events: 18 (down from 34 after provider reconfig)
- Evacuated hosts for maintenance: 24 hosts across 3 regions

Fleet / Capacity updates:
1) New capacity additions
  - us-west1: +2 H100 pods (6xA100 -> 4xH100 pods, completed 2026-10-08). Early benchmarks show ~1.6x throughput for long-context models.
  - eu-west1: +1 H100 pod (completed 2026-10-09); observed driver anomaly during initial rollout (see Incidents).
  - apac1: delayed arrival of reserved racks (logistics)  expected delivery 2026-10-19, impacting Dedicated commit ramp for APAC startups.
2) Decommission plan
  - a small set of older A100 PCIe hosts (36 nodes) scheduled for deprecation in q4 to make room for denser H100 hosting. Migration window: 2026-11-01 -> 2026-11-15.
3) Autoscaler and scheduling
  - Enabled improved scale-down cooldown (120s -> 420s) in apac1 and eu-west1 to prevent flapping for short-duration inference workloads. Initial results: 14% reduction in node churn, slight increase in idle GPU minutes.
  - Introduced best-effort bin-packing policy for Dedicated pools to ensure lower-latency models are scheduled on lower-utilization hosts.
4) Kernel/driver stack changes
  - Rolled CUDA 12.2 + NVIDIA driver 548.XX to us-west1 and apac1 with no regression. eu-west1 experienced a memory leak in the 548.XX driver under our long-run tests leading to a rollback to 545.XX while we coordinate with vendor.

Regions / routing / placement notes:
- Demand shift: eu-west1 request volume grew ~30% week-over-week driven by a single enterprise customer ramping production Dedicated usage. We coordinated with Sales to discuss priority routing and reserved capacity.
- APAC: trailing behind expected ramp due to rack delivery delays. Temporary routing policies have been applied to route latency-sensitive traffic for APAC customers through us-east1 with an SLA note to affected customers.
- Multi-region fallback: validated automatic fallback path for hosted chat customers in case of region saturation  average added latency measured ~220ms for eu->us failover.

Incidents and outages:
- 2026-10-09 eu-west1 driver regression (INC-2026-458): Deployment of NVIDIA 548.XX triggered progressive memory ballooning on a subset of H100 host images after ~48 hours under sustained KV-cache workloads. Impact: increased evictions and a spike in queue latency (p95 increased to 1.2s for ~3h).
  - Mitigation steps: rolled back to 545.XX within 3 hours, rebalanced pods, and quarantined affected host images for deeper profiling.
  - Action: vendor debug ticket opened with full heap traces (linked_artifacts includes the GitHub PR and Confluence notes).

Operational work completed this week:
- Completed rolling reboot and secure-boot validation on eu-west1 (post-drivers rollback).
- Finished migration of 18 Dedicated pools to new placement group logic (improved tail latency by ~12% for those pools).
- Autoscaler: introduced rate-limit on scale-up for non-critical hosted routes to mitigate spike-driven overprovisioning.

Open risks / blockers:
- Delivery delays in APAC racks threaten our Dedicated commitments for a specific enterprise customer with a 2026-10-25 deadline. Sales and Solutions Eng are engaged; contingency is to provide temporary reserved capacity in us-east1 or offer migration credits for early access to us-east1 capacity.
- GPU driver regression across vendor builds  until vendor provides a patch, we must maintain mixed-driver images per region which increases maintenance complexity and risk of inconsistent behavior across regions.
- Forecasted Q4 utilization could breach 90% in us-west1 if upcoming hosted promotions coincide with multiple Dedicated ramp-ups. Need to finalize short-term burst plan by 2026-10-16.

Planned work next week (2026-10-12 -> 2026-10-18):
- Finalize burst capacity plan for us-west1 and eu-west1 (Priya + Liam)  include temporary preemptible pools and reserved scheduling windows for critical Dedicated customers. Target: plan review 2026-10-15.
- Finish APAC rack intake process and perform early burn-in tests (Sofia)  target online date 2026-10-19.
- Deep memory-profiling of H100 images under sustained KV workloads (Ethan + vendor eng).
- Autoscaler: A/B test new scale-down policy with longer cooldowns on a non-critical pool (observability hooks to measure impact on cost and latency).
- Improve incident runbook for driver regressions: add immediate rollback checklist, post-mortem template, and automated host quarantine playbook.

Action items (owner):
- Priya: Draft burst capacity plan and escalate procurement options with cloud provider rep (due 2026-10-15).
- Liam: Coordinate with Sales on eu-west1 Dedicated priority list and implement per-customer routing tags (due 2026-10-14).
- Sofia: Track APAC rack shipment and provide daily intake updates; run burn-in validation suite once racks arrive (due 2026-10-19).
- Ethan: Complete memory-profiling and post results to the vendor ticket (JIRA-INFRA-2143) by 2026-10-16.

Notes / questions for broader eng leadership:
- Do we want to accelerate the A100->H100 decommission schedule given the utilization projections, or keep the buffer until after Nov holiday promotions? Tradeoff: cost savings vs. buffer for unexpected spikes.
- Sales: confirm which Dedicated customers must be prioritized for region-reserved capacity in APAC if racks are delayed.

Appendix:
- Short checklist for emergency rollback of drivers:
  1) Pause driver rollout.
  2) Mark affected images/hosts and trigger node drain with high-priority rescheduling.
  3) Roll back to last known-good driver and re-run our KV long-run test.
  4) Notify impacted customers via Ops channel and update status page.

- Quick links: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR/492 | Vendor ticket: internal-vendor-548-debug | Confluence: confluence:gpu-fleet-capacity-plans-2026

End of update.
